text:
**You need about 200 W of solar to refill a 1,000 Wh station in a day and a half, or about 300-350 W to do it in one sunny day.** Panels rarely deliver their rated watts, so the sources assume roughly 70-75% of the rating reaches the battery.

**The formula:** panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.75) ([power-runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)).

| Goal | Panel size |
|---|---|
| Full recharge in ~1.5 days (average US day, ~4.5 sun hours) | ~200 W. This yields about 630 Wh/day ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)) |
| Full recharge in 1 day, 6 sun hours | ~230 W ([power-runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)) |
| Full recharge in 1 day, 5 sun hours | ~270-300 W ([power-runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/), [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)) |
| Full recharge in 1 day, 4 sun hours | ~340 W ([power-runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)) |
| Full recharge in 1 day, northern winter | ~700 W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)) |

**Things that change the answer:**
- **Sun hours:** These are not daylight hours. Most of the US gets about 3-6 peak sun hours a day, and winter and cloudy regions fall at the low end ([SolarNiverse](https://solarniverse.com/chargers/charge-power-station-with-solar-panels/)).
- **Your station's solar input limit:** A station that accepts only 200 W won't use more, no matter how big the panel ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)). Mid-range 1,000-1,500 Wh units typically allow 400-800 W, but check your model ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Voltage:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside your station's input range. Exceeding it can damage the charge controller. If you use several panels, wiring them in series adds voltage, so check the combined Voc ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Running loads while charging:** Your net charge is solar input minus whatever you're drawing, so recharging takes longer.
- **Aiming:** Tilting panels toward the sun and re-aiming a few times a day can add 20-30% ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**A product option:** If your station accepts 400 W and a 12-60 V input, the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W Foldable Solar Panel](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) would refill 1,000 Wh in well under a day of good sun. The page lists it at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26. That link is an affiliate page. The panel's Voc is 45.3 V and it weighs 18.5 kg (about 41 lb), and it is too high-voltage for some small stations. Check your station's input specs before buying.

If you tell me your station model and where you live, I can narrow this to a specific panel size.
